name: Mike Pence
role: U.S. Representative (2001-2013), Governor of Indiana (2013-2017), Vice President (2017-2021); leads Advancing American Freedom
summary: A social and fiscal conservative and evangelical Christian who opposes abortion and same-sex marriage, favors low taxes, entitlement reform, school choice and a strong military. He has supported free trade and NATO and backed Ukraine, and since 2021 has broken with Trump over the 2020 election, tariffs and Ukraine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted against the Affordable Care Act and called for its repeal and defunding; has said healthcare should be a state matter and that Medicaid needs recipients to have skin in the game.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted against raising the federal minimum wage in 2007, signed a 2013 Indiana law barring local wage mandates, and has argued minimum-wage increases cost jobs.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Consistently backed free-market policy (tax cuts, free trade, opposing stimulus and bailouts) and has said socialism has failed everywhere.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge against new taxes, backed capital gains cuts and estate tax repeal, and favors lower taxes across the board.

unions-good.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted against Dodd-Frank, refused to comply with EPA rules, and as a candidate pledged to reverse Biden-era regulatory orders.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Supported the Patriot Act in 2001 and sponsored a 2009 bill extending several of its provisions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Called cannabis a gateway drug and opposed legalization; as governor reinstated mandatory minimums for some drug offenders and pledged to be tough on dealers.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed Indiana gun-friendly laws (guns in school-lot vehicles, manufacturer liability limits), backed a national concealed-carry standard and armed guards in schools.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pushed a dramatic defense spending increase as vice president, vowed to reverse a defense spending cut, and opposed defunding police.

decide-locally.rationale: Backed local control of education and state-level health policy, but also signed a law preempting local wage rules.

rehabilitation.rationale: Supported reentry programs (2007) but reinstated mandatory minimums for some drug offenders as governor; mixed.

traditional-family.rationale: Supported a constitutional amendment defining marriage as one man and one woman and has said he holds to traditional marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Backed a federal marriage amendment, opposed civil unions, and in the late 2010s-2022 reaffirmed support for marriage as one man and one woman while accepting the Obergefell ruling as law.

abortion-legal.rationale: Signed Indiana HEA 1337 (2016), supported overturning Roe, and in June 2023 urged every GOP candidate to back a nationwide ban before 15 weeks as a minimum.

more-religion-public.rationale: Calls religious freedom America's first freedom, backed repealing the Johnson Amendment and restoring religious protections in federal contracting.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Backed withholding UN funding until it becomes voluntary and program-specific (2011); no statement on UN power as such.

free-trade.rationale: Backed NAFTA, CAFTA, PNTR for China, the TPP and USMCA, and in 2025 called Trump's broad tariffs the largest peacetime tax hike; as VP he did impose China tariffs, which tempers it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported NATO action in Libya, safe zones in Syria and military action against ISIS; condemned Rohingya persecution.

open-borders.rationale: Calls border security the foundation of national security, declared the southern border a national emergency and opposes sanctuary cities.

limit-growth.rationale: Champions growth through tax cuts and an all-of-the-above energy strategy; rejects climate limits on the economy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate change not an emergency, opposed cap-and-trade, EPA greenhouse gas rules and the Clean Power Plan (Indiana sued).

central-planning.rationale: Has said socialism has failed everywhere it has been tried.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sought phase-out of the estate tax (2001) and in 2020 opposed taxing estates of the dead.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 argued tariffs are paid by importers and consumers and called the broad reciprocal tariffs a peacetime tax hike, while backing China-specific tariffs as VP; recent view leans against.

military-superiority.rationale: Backed a $716B defense increase, a Space Force and a dramatic military buildup against China and Russia as VP, and wanted a defense cut reversed in his 2024 plan.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Opposed equal-pay mandates arguing growth closes gaps and criticized quota-style civil rights laws.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Long stated an unbreakable bond with Israel and opposed a Palestinian state.

school-vouchers.rationale: Backed vouchers and parent choice among public, private and parochial schools as governor and in his 2023 campaign.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposed the 2009 stimulus, saying the $700B did not deliver, and preferred across-the-board tax relief; backed a balanced budget amendment.

reason-over-faith.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called Indiana a pro-coal state, backed Keystone XL and ANWR drilling, and pledged to reverse Biden energy orders and expand oil and gas leasing.

separated-powers.rationale: In his Jan. 6, 2021 letter said his oath barred him from unilaterally deciding electoral votes, and his group has urged Congress to reclaim tariff authority.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Supported NATO growth and a missile shield in Europe and America's leadership role in the free world.

death-penalty.rationale: Said he supports the death penalty and backed expedited executions for mass shooters in 2023.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Advocated teaching creationism alongside evolution in public schools.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Signed Indiana RFRA in 2015 and later backed religious protections in federal contracting; opposed reading RFRA as license for discrimination but backed exemptions.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Called climate science not a resolved issue and opposed EPA regulation of greenhouse gases.

collective-defense.rationale: Supports NATO and its expansion as central to American leadership.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Favors a flat federal tax rate and simplified code.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted against the 2008 TARP Wall Street bailout and stood against it as a lone Republican dissent per his later statements.

patriotic-education.rationale: His 2022 Freedom Agenda promoted "patriotic" education with heavier testing on the founding documents; it names no flag or anthem requirement.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Wrote in 2015 that he would veto any bill legalizing discrimination and signed the RFRA fix protecting sexual orientation and gender identity.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Said foreign investment benefits America but cited strengthened CFIUS review in his China speech.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Backed personal investment accounts for younger workers within Social Security.

single-official-language.rationale: Backed making English the official language of the United States (2007).

corporate-influence.rationale: Praised Citizens United and called McCain-Feingold oppressive.

non-intervention.rationale: Supported the Iraq war, Libya action, and arming Ukraine against Russia.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Supports NATO and American leadership alliances.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Opposed repealing Don't Ask, Don't Tell in 2010.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Backed the 2003 Iraq war and 2007 surge.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Signed the AFP No Climate Tax Pledge and opposed cap-and-trade.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Proposed a federal balanced budget amendment (2011) and pushed a state one in Indiana (2015).

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Defended Indiana right-to-work and said every American should be free to join a union or not.

voter-id.rationale: In 2026 he urged the Senate to make voter ID the law in all 50 states and to require photo ID or proof of citizenship at the ballot box; his 2022 Freedom Agenda also called for voter ID at the polls.

close-ties-china.rationale: His 2018 Hudson speech set out a confrontational China policy: tariffs, security and human-rights criticism, and rejection of reliance on Beijing.

multipolar-world.rationale: Champions American leadership of the free world and says Putin only understands strength.

notes: Recent clear positions govern: he opposes Trump's broad 2025 tariffs but backed China tariffs as VP. As governor he accepted Obergefell as law while personally keeping his traditional-marriage view. Many entries rely on secondary catalogs of his votes and statements; most votes are medium confidence.
